messages.subject: PCA and logit analysis
parts:
Hi everyone!  Im a little stuck as of late and think I know a way forward but wanted to get some input.  Hopefully I am on the right track.....

Some background:
I have a dataset of plots (Plot ID, latitude, longitude, elevation, slope, aspect, assignment) that has around 25000 observations but 2664 unique plots.  (Each observation is a plant species within the plot and has been categorized in the assignment column.)  I imported the 19 bioclim variables and matched them to the lat/long of my plots using the sp and raster packages.  I also removed duplicate plot observations so that I am only evaluating the 2664 unique plots in the principal components analysis.  So I ran the lat, long, slope, aspect, elevation variables plus all 19 bioclim variables through prcomp. (Assignment is dependent variable and Plot ID is just an identifier).  My result is that I decided to keep PC1, PC2, and PC3 as it explains 86% of the variation in the data.

Now, I need to extract PC1, PC2, and PC3 and use it in my model in a logit function.  I decided on a logit function because Assignment is categorical dependent variable (factor) with 6 levels although I only am interested in 2 of the levels.

My model should look like this:
Assignment ~ PC1 + PC2 + PC3
 
To run the new model using the 3PCs, I need to use the whole dataset with 25000 observations and extract the observations with the 2 levels of interest.
My immediate goal is to evaluate whether the 3 PCs are able to predict the correct Assignment.

So my questions are:
1) Will I have a problem using PC1, PC2 and PC3 in my logit model evaluating all 25000 observations (minus the 4 levels that are not of interest) if it was based on 2664 observations in the PCA?  Im thinking the length wont match in the evaluation of this but Im not sure.  Or should I have run the PCA on only the observations that I will be evaluating?
2) How do I extract PC1, PC2, and PC3 from the PCA to use in the model?
3)  Should I hold out some of my data so that there is a training set and a testing set?
4) Is there any obvious error in my thought process outlined above?  I am open to suggestions if there is a better way!


Thanks!
Jill
